subject: Geopolitics
title: Resource Curse
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Resource Curse.

hook.text: Nigeria earns billions from oil. Most Nigerians live on less than $2 a day. Wealth fuels corruption, not development.

buildup.text: The resource curse describes how natural wealth can weaken institutions. Leaders steal rather than build.

discovery.text: When revenue flows from resources rather than taxes, governments don't need citizens. Accountability vanishes.

twist.text: Norway escaped the curse through strong institutions built before oil was found. Sequence matters enormously.

climax.text: Resources don't doom a nation; but without institutions to manage wealth, riches accelerate dysfunction.

punchline.text: Oil in weak hands is not a blessing. It's a curse.

quiz.question: Why does resource wealth sometimes weaken states?
options: Governments don't need citizen taxes, so accountability fades
